credential_capture.label: Jellyfin sign-in details
credential_capture.description: Sign in with your normal Jellyfin username and password — you do not need to be a server admin. An admin API key is also accepted as an advanced/secondary option below, but a personal account cannot create one, so username+password is the option almost everyone should use.
credential_capture.submit_label: Create Jellyfin connection and start first sync

fields.name: base_url
fields.label: Jellyfin Server Base URL
fields.help_text: The base URL of your Jellyfin instance (e.g., https://jellyfin.example.com or http://192.168.1.100:8096).

fields.name: username
fields.label: Jellyfin Username
fields.help_text: Your normal Jellyfin sign-in username — the same one you use at /web/#/login on your server. Any account works, not just an admin. Leave both this and Password blank only if you're using the advanced API Key option below instead.

fields.name: password
fields.label: Jellyfin Password
fields.help_text: Your normal Jellyfin sign-in password. Sealed as a secret and used only to obtain a per-user access token — never logged or stored in plain text.

fields.name: secret
fields.label: Jellyfin API Key (advanced, admin-only)
fields.help_text: Advanced/secondary option: only a server administrator can generate this, under Dashboard > Advanced > API Keys (path: /web/#/dashboard/keys on your server). Most owners should use Username/Password above instead — a non-admin account cannot create an API key at all.

fields.name: jellyfin_user_id
fields.label: Jellyfin User ID or Username (advanced API Key option only)
fields.help_text: Only needed with the advanced API Key option: an API key authenticates to your server but does not identify a user, so if your server has more than one account you must say which one to collect as. Find your user id or username under Dashboard > Users (path: /web/#/dashboard/users on your server), or in your own profile page's URL. Not needed when signing in with Username/Password above — that already identifies you.

refresh_policy.rationale: Jellyfin is self-hosted with no public rate limits. Core API provides LastPlayedDate and PlayCount as aggregate state (not per-session history). Items are fetched as a full inventory snapshot each run (Jellyfin core API does not expose a true incremental cursor for items; only library-level metadata). Hourly polling is conservative and suitable for self-hosted deployments. v10.11.11 stable (2026-06-06). PlaybackReporting plugin is optional and marks v2 scope expansion; core v1 scope limited to aggregate playback metadata.

streams.name: libraries
streams.description: Jellyfin media libraries (Movies, TV Shows, Music, Collections, etc.). One record per library the user can access.

display.label: Your Jellyfin libraries
display.detail: Library names, types (Movies, Series, Music, etc.), and collection paths. Does not include individual items.

streams.name: items
streams.description: Items (content) across all Jellyfin libraries. Includes movies, TV episodes, music tracks, photos, etc. One record per item with current playback state (LastPlayedDate, PlayCount). Does not include session-level watch history—use PlaybackReporting plugin for that if available on your instance.

display.label: Your Jellyfin items
display.detail: Item names, types, library, playback state (LastPlayedDate, PlayCount, Played flag), genres, release date, and external provider IDs (IMDb, TVDB, TMDB). Cover art uploaded as blobs.
